quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Recipe Written Down] Even though the recipe has been in the family for three generations, Tia writes it down for the first time and hands copies to each of her cousins at the wedding.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Tia's reason for writing down the recipe?
options: She dislikes the recipe and wants it forgotten.
She wants to keep the recipe secret from her cousins.
She wants to make sure the tradition continues for future generations.
She plans to sell the recipe to a company.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants to make sure the tradition continues for future generations.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would finally write down and share something kept only in memory for generations.
quests.explanation: Writing it down for the first time and sharing it at a family event suggests Tia wants the tradition to be preserved and passed on.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Thinking It Over] The shopper adds the jacket to her cart, closes the browser, and returns three separate times over the next two days before finally completing the purchase.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the shopper's decision-making?
options: She decided instantly without any hesitation.
She regretted the purchase immediately afterward.
She never actually bought the jacket.
She thought carefully before committing to the purchase.
quests.correctAnswer: She thought carefully before committing to the purchase.
quests.hint: Think about what returning multiple times before buying suggests about how much thought went into the decision.
quests.explanation: Returning to the cart three times over two days before buying suggests the shopper carefully considered the purchase rather than deciding on impulse.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Extra Legroom] The airline seats Mr. Novak next to the emergency exit without being asked, and the flight attendant mentions it offers a bit more legroom for tall passengers.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Mr. Novak?
options: He complained about having too much space.
He requested a middle seat specifically.
He is likely taller than an average passenger.
He is shorter than most passengers.
quests.correctAnswer: He is likely taller than an average passenger.
quests.hint: Think about why the extra legroom detail is mentioned specifically in relation to him.
quests.explanation: Highlighting the extra legroom for tall passengers, right after seating him there, suggests Mr. Novak is likely taller than average.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Smiling Less] Ms. Anwar's therapist notices she smiles less during sessions lately and gently asks whether anything has changed at home or work recently.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the therapist's observation?
options: She thinks Ms. Anwar has been smiling more than usual.
She believes nothing has changed for Ms. Anwar.
She noticed a change in Ms. Anwar's mood over time.
She has never met Ms. Anwar before this session.
quests.correctAnswer: She noticed a change in Ms. Anwar's mood over time.
quests.hint: Think about what noticing 'less' smiling, compared to before, suggests about a change over time.
quests.explanation: Noticing that Ms. Anwar smiles less than she used to suggests the therapist has observed a shift in her mood recently.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [From Track Changes to 'Looks Good'] The intern's first draft comes back covered in track-changes, but by her fourth draft, her supervisor's only comment is 'looks good, send it.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the intern's writing over time?
options: It got worse with each draft.
It stayed exactly the same the whole time.
Her supervisor never actually read any of the drafts.
It improved significantly with practice.
quests.correctAnswer: It improved significantly with practice.
quests.hint: Compare the amount of feedback on the first draft with the supervisor's comment on the fourth.
quests.explanation: Going from heavy corrections to a simple 'looks good' suggests the intern's writing improved considerably across the drafts.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Full Study Room] Two weeks before finals, the study room that used to be empty every evening is now full of students by six o'clock.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the students' behavior before finals?
options: Fewer students are studying than before.
Students stopped using the room entirely.
The study room has been closed for renovations.
More of them are choosing to study in the evenings now.
quests.correctAnswer: More of them are choosing to study in the evenings now.
quests.hint: Compare how full the room used to be with how full it is now, and think about the timing.
quests.explanation: A once-empty study room filling up two weeks before finals suggests more students are dedicating evenings to studying as the exams approach.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Removing a Dish] The chef removes the fish dish from the menu after three customers in one week ask for it well-done rather than the traditional preparation.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the chef's decision?
options: The traditional preparation was not matching customer expectations.
Every customer loved the traditional preparation.
The chef ran out of fish permanently.
The dish was too popular to keep making.
quests.correctAnswer: The traditional preparation was not matching customer expectations.
quests.hint: Think about why repeated requests to change how a dish is cooked might lead a chef to remove it instead.
quests.explanation: Repeated requests to change the preparation suggest the traditional style was not matching what several customers wanted, leading the chef to remove it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Still Talking About the Ending] The independent film wins no major awards, but three different critics write follow-up articles months later, still discussing its ending.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the film's impact?
options: It left a lasting impression despite not winning awards.
It was completely forgotten right after release.
It was widely regarded as a failure.
Critics refused to discuss it at all.
quests.correctAnswer: It left a lasting impression despite not winning awards.
quests.hint: Think about what critics still writing about it months later suggests, even without award wins.
quests.explanation: Critics still discussing the film's ending months later suggests it made a lasting impression, even without winning major awards.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Moving to a Bigger Field] The town's annual festival moves to a bigger field this year after last year's location ran out of parking spaces by early afternoon.
quests.question: What can be inferred about last year's festival attendance?
options: It was larger than the original location could comfortably handle.
The festival was cancelled last year.
No one attended the festival last year.
It was smaller than expected.
quests.correctAnswer: It was larger than the original location could comfortably handle.
quests.hint: Think about what running out of parking by early afternoon suggests about how many people came.
quests.explanation: Running out of parking early, followed by a move to a bigger field, suggests last year's turnout exceeded what the original location could handle.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Steps in Large Letters] The grandmother asks her grandson to write down the steps for video-calling in large letters, then tapes the paper next to the tablet.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the grandmother?
options: She plans to give the tablet away.
She wants to be able to make video calls on her own in the future.
She has no interest in ever using the tablet.
She already knows every step by heart.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants to be able to make video calls on her own in the future.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would want written steps taped somewhere they can see them repeatedly.
quests.explanation: Asking for written steps kept nearby suggests the grandmother wants to be able to make the calls herself going forward.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Recycled Wrapping] Every gift under the tree this year is wrapped in the same recycled paper, and the tags are made from cut-up cereal boxes instead of store-bought labels.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the family's approach to gift-giving this year?
options: They received the gifts from a store already wrapped.
They are trying to reduce waste and reuse materials.
They forgot to buy wrapping paper this year.
They dislike giving gifts to each other.
quests.correctAnswer: They are trying to reduce waste and reuse materials.
quests.hint: Think about what reused materials for wrapping and tags suggest about their values this year.
quests.explanation: Using recycled paper and cereal-box tags instead of store-bought materials suggests the family is intentionally trying to reduce waste.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Well-Chosen Sample] The store clerk hands the customer a sample of the new cheese before he even asks, mentioning that it pairs well with the wine already in his basket.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the clerk?
options: She is trying to prevent him from buying wine.
She offers samples to no one in the store.
She is unaware of what he put in his basket.
She paid attention to what he had already selected.
quests.correctAnswer: She paid attention to what he had already selected.
quests.hint: Think about how the clerk knew to connect the cheese sample to something specific in his basket.
quests.explanation: Connecting the cheese sample to the wine already in his basket shows the clerk noticed his selections and tailored her suggestion.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Lingering After the Meeting] After the presentation, three senior partners linger in the room asking Amara follow-up questions, while everyone else has already filed out to lunch.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the senior partners' interest in Amara's presentation?
options: They found it completely uninteresting.
They had already heard the same information before.
They wanted to leave as quickly as possible.
It captured their attention more than a typical presentation.
quests.correctAnswer: It captured their attention more than a typical presentation.
quests.hint: Think about what staying behind to ask more questions, while others leave, suggests about their engagement.
quests.explanation: Senior partners staying behind with follow-up questions, while others leave for lunch, suggests Amara's presentation stood out to them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Weekend Visitor Log] The hiking trail's visitor log shows dozens of names each weekend, but on weekdays, sometimes an entire week passes with only two or three entries.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the trail's popularity?
options: No one visits the trail at any time.
It receives the same number of visitors every day.
It is more popular on weekdays than weekends.
It is far more popular on weekends than on weekdays.
quests.correctAnswer: It is far more popular on weekends than on weekdays.
quests.hint: Compare the number of entries on weekends with the number during the week.
quests.explanation: Dozens of weekend entries compared to just a few during the week suggest the trail is much more popular on weekends.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Glass of Water Before Meals] Since Mr. Petrov started drinking a full glass of water before every meal, his doctor notes that his usual afternoon headaches have not come up in his last two visits.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the connection between the new habit and his headaches?
options: The new habit made his headaches worse.
His headaches never actually improved.
The two things are completely unrelated.
The new habit may have helped reduce his headaches.
quests.correctAnswer: The new habit may have helped reduce his headaches.
quests.hint: Think about what the doctor noticing this change, right after the new habit started, suggests.
quests.explanation: Headaches no longer coming up at his last two visits, after he started the new habit, suggests it may have helped reduce them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Names from a Hat] The teacher assigns partners for the science project by drawing names from a hat instead of letting students choose, explaining only that 'it worked better last year.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about how students chose partners in previous years?
options: Letting students choose their own partners caused some problem.
Students were always assigned partners randomly before.
Every student was thrilled with their partner every year.
The teacher has never assigned a group project before.
quests.correctAnswer: Letting students choose their own partners caused some problem.
quests.hint: Think about what 'it worked better last year' implies about how the earlier method compared.
quests.explanation: Saying the new method 'worked better last year' suggests letting students pick their own partners had caused some kind of issue previously.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Extra Matinees] The theater keeps adding extra matinee showings of the play, and the box office reports that most of them sell out within a day of being announced.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the demand for the play?
options: The play has stopped attracting audiences.
It is lower than the theater expected.
It exceeds what the original schedule could accommodate.
Tickets remain available for weeks after each showing.
quests.correctAnswer: It exceeds what the original schedule could accommodate.
quests.hint: Think about what needing extra showings, which then sell out quickly, suggests about demand.
quests.explanation: Extra showings that sell out within a day suggest audience demand is higher than the theater's original schedule could handle.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Surprise for Everyone] Dad quietly pays off the layaway item at the store without telling anyone, then acts surprised along with everyone else when it is opened on the holiday.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Dad's behavior?
options: He wants everyone to know it was his idea.
He forgot that he paid for the item.
He wants the gift to feel like a surprise, even for himself.
He genuinely does not know what the gift is.
quests.correctAnswer: He wants the gift to feel like a surprise, even for himself.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would hide their own involvement in a gift they already paid for.
quests.explanation: Pretending to be surprised, despite having paid for the gift himself, shows Dad wants to preserve the fun of the surprise for everyone, including himself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Motion-Sensor Lights] The neighborhood watch group adds motion-sensor lights to three streets after a string of package thefts reported over the winter.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the motion-sensor lights?
options: They were installed to save on the electric bill.
They are meant to attract more visitors to the area.
They are intended to help prevent further thefts.
They were added purely for decoration.
quests.correctAnswer: They are intended to help prevent further thefts.
quests.hint: Think about the connection between the recent thefts and the type of lights chosen.
quests.explanation: Installing motion-sensor lights right after a string of thefts suggests the group hopes the lights will help deter further incidents.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Crashes After an Update] The app's crash reports spike right after the newest phone model is released, though the app works fine on every older device tested.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the app's issue?
options: It has never worked on any device.
It works better on the newest phone than older ones.
The crashes are unrelated to any specific device.
It may not be fully compatible with the newest phone model yet.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not be fully compatible with the newest phone model yet.
quests.hint: Compare how the app performs on older devices with how it performs right after the new phone's release.
quests.explanation: Crashes spiking specifically after the new model's release, while older devices work fine, suggest a compatibility issue with the newest phone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sticking to the List] The shopper brings a printed list into the store, checks off each item with a pen, and walks past the snack aisle without stopping even once.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the shopper's trip?
options: She spent most of her time in the snack aisle.
She is sticking closely to a planned shopping list.
She forgot to bring a list.
She is buying items at random.
quests.correctAnswer: She is sticking closely to a planned shopping list.
quests.hint: Think about what checking off items and skipping an entire aisle suggests about her approach to shopping.
quests.explanation: Checking off a printed list and skipping the snack aisle entirely suggests the shopper is disciplined about sticking to her plan.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Text Reminders] Since the clinic began sending appointment reminders by text instead of only by mail, the number of missed appointments has fallen by nearly half.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the mailed reminders?
options: They worked better than the text reminders.
They were sent more frequently than the texts.
They were less effective at reaching patients in time.
They had no effect on missed appointments.
quests.correctAnswer: They were less effective at reaching patients in time.
quests.hint: Compare the missed-appointment rate before and after the switch to texting.
quests.explanation: Missed appointments falling by nearly half after switching to texts suggests the mailed reminders were less effective at reaching patients.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Flipping Through the Pages] The border agent stamps everyone's passport quickly until she reaches Mr. Haddad's, pausing to flip through several pages before finally stamping it as well.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Mr. Haddad's passport?
options: It was rejected by the agent.
It likely contains more stamps or travel history than the others.
It was completely blank inside.
It belonged to someone else entirely.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely contains more stamps or travel history than the others.
quests.hint: Think about what would make an agent pause and flip through more pages for one traveler.
quests.explanation: Pausing to flip through several pages, compared to quickly stamping everyone else's, suggests Mr. Haddad's passport has more travel history to look through.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Quiet Group Chat] The team's group chat goes quiet for the first time in weeks after the Friday announcement that the project has been placed on hold indefinitely.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the team's reaction to the announcement?
options: They had already expected this exact outcome for weeks.
They were thrilled by the announcement.
The news likely caught them off guard or disappointed them.
The chat was always quiet regardless of any news.
quests.correctAnswer: The news likely caught them off guard or disappointed them.
quests.hint: Think about what a sudden silence, right after previously being very active, suggests about the team's reaction.
quests.explanation: A chat that suddenly goes quiet right after this news, after being active for weeks, suggests the announcement surprised or disappointed the team.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Snacks from Home] The cafeteria removes fried options from the menu, and within the month, students start bringing more snacks from home than they ever did before.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the students' reaction to the menu change?
options: Every student preferred the new healthier menu immediately.
The change had no effect on student behavior.
Students stopped eating at school entirely.
Some students were not satisfied with the new options.
quests.correctAnswer: Some students were not satisfied with the new options.
quests.hint: Think about what an increase in outside snacks, right after the menu change, suggests about satisfaction.
quests.explanation: More students bringing snacks from home right after fried options were removed suggests some were not fully satisfied with the new menu.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Waiting for Uncle Marco] Every year, Uncle Marco arrives at the family dinner exactly one hour late, yet everyone waits to start eating until he walks through the door.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the family's feelings toward Uncle Marco?
options: They start eating early to avoid him.
They are annoyed and refuse to wait for him.
They have stopped inviting him to dinners.
They value his presence enough to wait for him.
quests.correctAnswer: They value his presence enough to wait for him.
quests.hint: Think about why a family would consistently delay a meal for one specific person.
quests.explanation: Consistently waiting to eat until Uncle Marco arrives suggests the family values having him there enough to hold off on the meal.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Notes for the Substitute] The substitute teacher receives a folder full of detailed lesson notes, sticky tabs marking each page, and a separate sheet listing which students need extra support.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the regular teacher who prepared these materials?
options: She rarely plans ahead for her classes.
She left no information for the substitute.
She is very thorough and considerate in her planning.
She dislikes having substitute teachers.
quests.correctAnswer: She is very thorough and considerate in her planning.
quests.hint: Think about what this level of detailed preparation reveals about the regular teacher's habits.
quests.explanation: Providing detailed notes, tabs, and a support list for the substitute shows the regular teacher is thorough and considerate in her planning.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Three Songs Every Night] The band's setlist changes slightly every night of the tour, but three particular songs appear in every single show without exception.
quests.question: What can be inferred about those three songs?
options: They are likely considered essential to the band's performance.
They are the band's least favorite songs to play.
They were removed from the tour entirely.
They are only played on request from fans.
quests.correctAnswer: They are likely considered essential to the band's performance.
quests.hint: Think about what appearing in every show, while other songs rotate, suggests about their importance.
quests.explanation: Appearing in every single show, while the rest of the setlist changes, suggests these three songs are considered essential to the performance.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Eye-Level Displays] The boutique's owner rearranges the window display every Monday morning, always placing the newest arrivals at eye level facing the street.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the owner's strategy?
options: She never changes the display at all.
She places the oldest items at eye level.
She wants passersby to notice the newest items first.
She wants to hide the newest items from view.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants passersby to notice the newest items first.
quests.hint: Think about why placing new items at eye level facing the street would matter for a shop owner.
quests.explanation: Placing the newest arrivals at eye level facing the street suggests the owner wants to catch the attention of people walking by.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Second Ticket Window] The community theater's ticket booth adds a second window this season after last year's opening-night line stretched around the block.
quests.question: What can be inferred about last year's opening night?
options: Very few people showed up to buy tickets.
Attendance was higher than the booth could handle smoothly.
Tickets were available only online last year.
The theater was closed on opening night.
quests.correctAnswer: Attendance was higher than the booth could handle smoothly.
quests.hint: Think about what a line stretching around the block suggests about how many people came, and why a second window was added.
quests.explanation: A line stretching around the block, followed by the addition of a second ticket window, suggests attendance exceeded what one window could handle.
